newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss unveil new anti-forgery 20-franc note.
newsitem.headline: Swiss unveil new anti-forgery 20-franc note.

text.p: Switzerland on Wednesday unveiled a new state-of-the-art 20-franc note aimed at foiling forgers which will begin circulation on October 1.
The Swiss National Bank (SNB) presented facsimiles of the note to journalists, which follows introduction of a 50-franc note last year. Other denominations will follow in the next two years.

The notes are designed to be nearly impossible to counterfeit. Features include a "magic" numeral in transparent ink, as well as shimmering chameleon-like numerals on the bill face which change colour.
The new high-tech notes, featuring Swiss composer Arthus Honegger, cost 30 centimes to print, compared to 20 centimes for the old versions.
Since the new 50-franc bills were introduced last year, the SNB has found only one case of counterfeiting, said SNB vice chairman Jean-Pierre Roth.
The SNB has so far had few complaints about the new note series from cash-loving Swiss.

"People are very oriented towards cash," said Roland Tornare, chief cashier of the SNB. He said complaints had included one from a woman who tried to iron the new 50 and found it melted due to the special materials.
"We advised her to use the silk setting on the iron," he said.
